dedupe_keys.name: gsma renewable energy dashboard for mobile towers

description: The GSMA Renewable Energy Dashboard maps how mobile towers in low- and middle-income countries are powered. It gives detailed figures for 20 countries and high-level summaries for about 70 more, covering tower locations or counts, the number of towers running on on-site renewable energy, the numbers of off-grid sites (not connected to the grid) and bad-grid sites (connected but without grid power for more than six hours a day on average), and emissions from diesel generators. It was built by the GSMA's Mobile for Development team, which has tracked renewable power for towers since its Green Power for Mobile work and a 2014 report, and is accompanied by reports on how tower companies, energy service companies and new technology are changing the picture; GSMA notes that better grid access has reduced the number of off-grid sites and slowed renewable investment. Coverage: low- and middle-income countries in Africa, Asia and Latin America, with estimates for recent years. Format and access: interactive web dashboard with country pages, free to view; downloads and licence terms were not visible because the site refused automated access. Caveats: many figures are modelled estimates from industry sources; the dashboard has been rebuilt and may change. Simulation uses: resource potential and backup power options for cell sites, dependence of mobile networks on unreliable grids and diesel supply, and emissions scenarios. Related records: the ITU 5G base station energy dataset gives site-level consumption, and the World Bank resilient telecom guide covers power backup measures.
